newsitem.title: USA: CalPERS says portfolio value jumps to $113 bln.
newsitem.headline: CalPERS says portfolio value jumps to $113 bln.

text.p: California's Public Employees' Retirement System -- the nation's largest public pension fund -- said Wednesday its portfolio was now valued at $113 billion, up from $108 billion at the end of March.

The CalPERS investment portfolio suffered a $2 billion drop in value in March due to declines in the U.S. stock and bond markets. But the fund said it quickly recovered the losses, gaining $5 billion since March to reach an all time high of $113 billion as of May 19.

"Today's announcement is evidence that CalPERS' long-term investment strategy is sound and positions the Fund to grow steadily over time," said Charles Valdes, who chairs the fund's investment committee.

CalPERS said 64 percent of its assets are currently invested in equities, 30 percent in fixed income and 6 percent in real estate. For the year ending March 31, the fund said it earned an 11 percent return on its investments.
CalPERS is the nation's largest public pension fund and third largest in the world. It provides retirement and health benefits to more than one million public employees and their families.
